executive_summary: As of 25 January 2027, the expiration of the Orvan Grain Corridor Agreement on 10 September 2026 has resulted in significant trade exposure for Midgard and Tolan. Midgard wheat imports from Orvan fell by USD 156.5M to USD 216.2M YoY in the months following expiration. Midgard's maize imports saw a delayed impact due to contractual terms, eventually dropping by over USD 100M YoY in late Q4. Tolan's wheat imports were similarly impacted, showing a deficit of USD 69.6M to USD 96.0M. In all cases, while alternative shipments from Vanir and rail routes provided some relief, they remained small in scale compared to the lost maritime volumes from Orvan and were often more expensive to handle.

Midgard buyers had expected the corridor agreement to be renewed. It expired on 10 September without a replacement.

outlook.text: The outlook for Q1 2027 remains constrained. Without a renewal of the corridor agreement or a massive scale-up in alternative logistics (rail or Vanir supply), import volumes for wheat and maize are expected to remain at these depressed levels. High handling costs for substitute supplies will likely continue to pressure grain millers and industrial buyers in Midgard and Tolan.
assumptions: No new maritime corridor agreement is reached in early 2027.
Vanir supply remains stable but limited by current logistical capacity.
Rail routes continue to operate at high capacity but cannot fully replace lost sea volumes.
